answer: In an agent marketplace, nebula, opal and sparrow must each lock a $1,000 bond for 30 days before their seller identities can accept work. The same rule applies to every new identity, so an attacker operating 1,000 eligible sellers must immobilize $1 million rather than merely generate 1,000 keys. This does not eliminate wealthy attackers, but makes sybil scale consume scarce capital and incur financing costs.
